Subject: API latency and 502s observed from eastus2-AZ5 — urgent

Kimberly / team,

We're seeing a sustained increase in p95/p99 latency and a spike in 502s originating from eastus2-AZ5 beginning ~08:50 PDT. Throughput for our traffic to your API has dropped ~45% and error rate is at ~6% over the last 25 minutes. This is impacting checkout flows and our SLIs.

Examples (UTC timestamps):
- 2028-08-17T16:51:02Z — 502 on /v1/generate (latency 1.8s)
- 2028-08-17T16:57:44Z — 504 on /v1/embeddings (latency 2.3s)

We attempted retry logic on our side but we're still seeing progressive failures. Can you confirm if there's an AZ-level outage or throttling? Our SREs are standing by; we'd appreciate an ETA and whether you intend to fail traffic over.

Attaching a short sample of request/response pairs and edge timestamps.

Attachments: ventana_sample_logs.txt (attached)

Thanks,
Samir
Senior Platform Engineer 
Ventana

Samir — thanks for the heads-up and the logs. We're activating an incident bridge now and prioritizing this for immediate mitigation. Short answers up front:
1) We see elevated 5xx rates tied to eastus2-AZ5 and a correlated spike in backend KV cache pressure.
2) We're initiating a prioritized cross-region routing change (traffic pin / policy override) to shift Ventana traffic to eastus3 and us-west2 while the AZ stabilizes.
3) We'll follow up with a timeline and a postmortem.

Immediate action plan (next 90 min):
- Engineering (Markus) will post a technical update and enact routing override.
- Ops will enable short-lived model variant fallback to lower memory pressure.
- I'm coordinating an executive comms note and a one-time credit proposal if this hits your SLA threshold.

I'll update you in the next 10–15 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we know this is high impact.

Attachments: route-change-runbook.md (internal runbook link)

—
Kimberly Park

Cc: Samir Patel <samir@ventana.io>, rachel.kim@redwood.com, eng-oncall@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-17T09:26:30-07:00
Subject: Re: API latency and 502s observed from eastus2-AZ5 — urgent

Posting rapid technical update from the bridge. TL;DR: KV cache saturation on AZ5 causing serialization at the runtime layer and a shortfall in worker availability for continuous batching. Error pattern: elevated 502/504 with increased tail latency (p99 ~2.4s).

Observed metrics (Ventana traffic slice, last 15m):
- p50 120ms, p95 540ms, p99 2.4s
- 5xx rate 5.9% (baseline <0.2%)
- Worker queue depth scaling up without proportional capacity due to memory pressure (KV miss-to-load spike).

Mitigation steps executed (09:20–09:25 PDT):
- Enabled model-variant fallback for Ventana (lighter quantized replica) to reduce per-request memory footprint.
- Triggered routing policy override (priority: ram-pressure-evacuate) to shift 70% of Ventana traffic to eastus3 and 30% to us-west2.
- Warmed prefix cache on the recipient regions to avoid cold-start penalty.

Attachments: route-change-runbook.md (applied runbook), ventana_sample_logs.txt (customer-provided).

Next: watching for error-rate decay; if 5xx does not fall <0.5% in 15m we will escalate to cross-region full evacuation and open an AWS support case for AZ5 fabric checks. I've also opened PD incident PD-789123.

—Markus
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Samir — quick update from the bridge and a next-steps checklist.

Status: at 12:50 PDT we completed the prioritized routing override. Current telemetry for Ventana traffic: p95 ~280ms, p99 ~640ms, 5xx ~0.3%. Throughput has returned to within 95% of baseline.

What we did:
- Shifted traffic to eastus3/us-west2 with warmed caches to minimize cold-starts.
- Enabled a lighter model variant for short windows to reduce KV memory pressure.
- Engaged AWS for AZ5 fabric validation (support case opened; AWS oncall looped).

Customer commitments:
- Immediate: keep the route override for 4 hours while we validate AZ5 stability.
- Short-term: postmortem and RCA within 48 hours; we'll include mitigation actions (routing guardrails, pre-warm policies, KV capacity thresholds).
- Commercial: offered a one-time 10% credit for August invoice (DocuSign link below).
